definition: Exhaustion of administrative remedies is a doctrine that generally requires a party to fully pursue all administrative remedies available when challenging a Federal agency’s decision prior to seeking a judicial remedy. This allows for a more efficient judicial system and synced administrative state. Exhausting of administrative remedies prevents cases from clogging the court system or resulting in different judicially defined rules for each controversy. Generally, a person who has an issue with an administrative rule or statute must go to the agency that created it first. The agency usually has their own review process like filing grievances through the form of a petition, then holding a hearing, and an internal appeal process, if available. Under the exhaustion of administrative remedies doctrine, only after a person completes (exhausts) all of the agency’s available steps, then they may pursue litigation. See: Administrative Procedure Act, 5 U.S.C. § 552, and 5 U.S.C. 704.
